transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve been eating way too much after my late shifts. I’ll get takeout, then come home and keep eating—chips, sweets, whatever’s around. Afterwards I look at how much I had and I’m kind of shocked.
After eating like that, do you ever do anything to try to counteract the food, such as making yourself throw up or taking laxatives?
Sometimes, yeah. After I’ve eaten a lot, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just don’t want it sitting in me and turning into weight.
Could you tell me your current height and weight?
I’m not sure of my exact weight right now. I haven’t checked recently.
On average, how many times a week do you find yourself eating this way and throwing up?

Most weeks, at least once. Since I got settled after moving, it’s kind of become a routine—I'll eat too much late at night, then throw up, or sometimes skip breakfast or make myself go for a long run afterward.
Roughly how many months has this routine been going on?
About a year and five months, I think—since I moved into that temporary apartment near the tourist district.
Would you or your doctors consider your current body weight to be significantly underweight for your height?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been weighing myself, and no doctor has told me that I’m underweight.
How much does your body shape or weight influence how you feel about yourself as a person?
I’m not sure how much it does. I mean, I do think about my weight sometimes, but I haven’t really thought of it as affecting how I feel about myself overall.
During these times when you are eating late at night, do you feel like you cannot stop eating or cannot control what or how much you are eating?
Yes. Once I start, it feels like I can’t make myself stop. I’m telling myself to put it away, but I just keep opening more containers until it’s all gone.
Do you have an intense fear or dread of gaining weight or becoming fat?

Yeah, I do. Even though people at the venue sometimes say I look too lean, I get really panicky if my pants feel even a little tighter or the scale goes up a pound. I worry guests or coworkers will notice right away and think I’ve let myself go.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past several months or year?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed any major weight loss over the past year.
Do these episodes of overeating and making yourself throw up happen two or more times a week on average?
Since the move settled down, it’s usually at least once a week. I’ll eat way more than I meant to, then try to make up for it by throwing up, skipping breakfast, or making myself go for a long run.
I don’t have a specific number that I’m trying to stay under. I just get anxious when the scale goes up.
